title: In a normal extension, the roots of a minimal polynomial are conjugate under automorphisms (Stacks 0BME (2))
statement: Let $F$ be a field and $E/F$ a field extension [def-pc-field-extension] which is algebraic and normal: every $\alpha\in E$ is algebraic over $F$ [def-weil-algebraic-element] and its minimal polynomial over $F$ [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension] is a product of polynomials of degree one in $E[T]$. Let $\alpha\in E$ with minimal polynomial $P\in F[T]$ over $F$, and let $\beta\in E$ with $P(\beta)=0$. Then there is an $F$-algebra automorphism $\sigma$ of $E$ with $\sigma(\alpha)=\beta$.

mathlib_searches.query: normal extension: two elements with the same minimal polynomial are conjugate by an automorphism
In a normal field extension E/F, if y is a root of the minimal polynomial of x then some F-automorphism of E sends x to y
